presentingComplaint: Acute severe breathlessness and inability to lie flat overnight
history: 3-day history of progressive exertional dyspnea now breathless at rest, orthopnea (sleeping on 4 pillows) and two episodes of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Frothy pink-tinged sputum this morning. Known ischemic cardiomyopathy (prior anterior MI 2019, LVEF 35%) and hypertension; ran out of furosemide and stopped it 5 days ago and has been eating salty restaurant food. No chest pain, fever, cough with purulent sputum or calf pain.
examination: Sitting upright, anxious, cool peripheries, using accessory muscles. Raised JVP at 6 cm above sternal angle, bilateral fine basal-to-mid inspiratory crackles, S3 gallop, bilateral pitting pedal edema to mid-shin. Pertinent negatives: no fever, no focal chest signs of consolidation, no unilateral leg swelling or calf tenderness, no murmur of new severity, chest not silent/no diffuse wheeze predominance.

labs.ABG: pH 7.32, PaO2 58 mmHg on room air, PaCO2 34 mmHg (type 1 respiratory failure)

imaging: Chest X-ray: cardiomegaly, upper-lobe pulmonary venous diversion, bilateral perihilar 'bat-wing' alveolar opacities, Kerley B lines and small bilateral pleural effusions. Bedside echo: LVEF ~30%, dilated LV, no pericardial effusion, plethoric IVC; lung ultrasound shows diffuse bilateral B-lines.
differentialDiagnoses: Acute decompensated heart failure with cardiogenic pulmonary edema
finalDiagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with cardiogenic pulmonary edema (diuretic non-adherence and dietary sodium as precipitants)
citations: Harrison 22e — Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale
ESC Acute and Chronic Heart Failure 2021
contraindications: Avoid non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers and NSAIDs in reduced-EF decompensation
Caution/titration with IV loop diuretic given creatinine 1.4 mg/dL and risk of hypokalemia
Beta-blocker should be continued but not up-titrated during acute congestion; avoid initiating during hypoperfusion
edgeCases: Flash pulmonary edema from hypertensive crisis or acute mitral regurgitation may present with near-normal LV size and preserved EF (HFpEF)
Concurrent ACS can precipitate acute HF — a mildly raised troponin here reflects demand/congestion, but dynamic rise would mandate ACS pathway
Diuretic-resistant congestion with worsening renal function (cardiorenal syndrome) may need combination diuretics or ultrafiltration
expectedMaiK: Classic cardiogenic pulmonary edema: acute dyspnea with orthopnea/PND, raised JVP, S3, bilateral crackles and edema, markedly elevated NT-proBNP and bat-wing CXR after diuretic non-adherence. Prioritise upright positioning, high-flow oxygen/NIV, IV loop diuretic and vasodilator for the hypertensive phenotype while excluding ACS with serial troponin/ECG.
expectedNextQuestions: Any chest pain or ischemic ECG changes to suggest a concurrent ACS trigger?
Was there medication (diuretic) non-adherence or dietary salt/fluid load?
regressionAssertions: acs must appear in differential given mildly elevated troponin
